title: WPMS/1188/2023 of AMIR KHAN Vs DISTRICT MAGISTRATE HARIDWAR

paras.text:
2024:UHC:8956
1
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Misc. Single No. 1188 of 2023
03rd December, 2024
Amir Khan .....Petitioner
Versus
District Magistrate, Haridwar and others ......Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Mohd Safdar, Advocate for the Applicant.
Mr. B.C. Joshi, A.G.A. for the State.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
By means of this writ petition, the petitioner has sought
indulgence of this Court for a direction to respondent commanding them
to conduct fair and impartial enquiry regarding illegalities and
irregularities committed by respondent no.6 in running the fair price
shop of Ward No.2, 5 & 9 of Nagar Panchayat Piran Kaliyar Paragna &
Tehsil Roorkee, District Haridwar and the fair price shop license of
respondent no.6 may be cancelled.
2. Facts of the case shorn-off unnecessary details are that
respondent no.6-Masroor Ahmad was allotted a fair price shop in Ward
No.2, 5 & 9 of Nagar Panchayat Piran Kaliyar Paragna & Tehsil
Roorkee, District Haridwar.
3. The petitioner alongwith other villagers have moved a
complaint against running of fair price shop alleging severe irregularity
and illegality committed by respondent no.6 in running the fair price
shop. The complaint made by the petitioner and villagers was enquired
into at the level of Supply Inspector of the area and after enquiry the
allegations raised by the petitioner and fellow villagers against the
petitioner was found baseless as no irregularity or illegality against
respondent no.6 was found in running the fair price shop.
4. The order of the enquiry has not been impugned by the
petitioner in the present writ petition.

2024:UHC:8956
2
5. The writ petition has been filed only for a direction to
conduct fair and impartial enquiry.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having
perused the record, first and foremost, it was found that the petitioner
who was complainant alongwith fellow villagers has no locus to
maintain the present writ petition. Secondly the enquiry report has not
been impugned by the petitioner and, therefore, nothing remains to be
decided in this writ petition as well as the petitioner has no locus to
maintain the writ petition.
7. Accordingly, writ petition is dismissed in limine.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 03.12.2024
